general.q: Which desert is widely considered the driest non-polar desert in the world?
general.why: Parts of Chile's Atacama Desert have had no recorded rainfall for centuries.

general.q: Which is the most abundant chemical element in the universe by mass?
general.why: Hydrogen accounts for roughly 75% of all normal matter in the cosmos.

general.q: Which citrus fruit provides the distinctive flavouring in Earl Grey tea?
general.why: Bergamot oil is extracted from the rinds of the fragrant bergamot orange.

general.q: In snooker, how many points are awarded for potting the blue ball?
general.why: Colours run from yellow (2) through green (3), brown (4), blue (5), pink (6), to black (7).

general.q: Which English computer scientist invented the World Wide Web in 1989?
general.why: He invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN in Geneva.

pop.q: In the comedy series I'm Alan Partridge, what is the first name of Alan's long-suffering personal assistant?
pop.why: Played by Felicity Montagu, Lynn patiently endured Alan's bizarre antics and demands.

pop.q: Which car model was advertised in the 1990s in a famous TV campaign starring the characters Papa and Nicole?
pop.why: The French-themed commercials were huge hits in the UK, running from 1991 to 1998.

pop.q: Which Scottish developer, based in Dundee, created the hit 1991 puzzle video game Lemmings?
pop.why: DMA Design later created Grand Theft Auto and rebranded as Rockstar North.

pop.q: What paperwork famously came included with every Cabbage Patch Kids doll sold during the 1980s craze?
pop.why: Each doll was marketed as unique and came complete with an adoption certificate.

pop.q: In the 1988 action film Die Hard, what is the name of the Los Angeles skyscraper seized by Hans Gruber?
pop.why: Filming took place at Fox Plaza, the real-life headquarters of 20th Century Fox.

music.q: Which 1981 UK number one single by Soft Cell was originally recorded by Gloria Jones in 1964?
music.why: Gloria Jones recorded 'Tainted Love' in 1964 as a B-side before Soft Cell turned it into a hit.

music.q: Which acid jazz band's 1996 video for 'Virtual Insanity' featured lead singer Jay Kay on a moving floor?
music.why: The iconic music video won four MTV Video Music Awards in 1997, including Video of the Year.

music.q: What was the title of Scottish rock band The Fratellis' hit debut studio album, released in 2006?
music.why: Costello Music debuted at number two on the UK Albums Chart and sold over a million copies.

music.q: Which song gave the UK its first ever victory in the Eurovision Song Contest in 1967?
music.why: Performed barefoot by Sandie Shaw, 'Puppet on a String' won Eurovision by a massive landslide.

music.q: Which Scottish band released the critically acclaimed 1997 album 'White On Blonde'?
music.why: White On Blonde contained hit singles like 'Say What You Want' and went six times platinum in the UK.

mix.q: Which British band had a major UK hit in 1995 with the anthem 'Alright'?
mix.why: 'Alright' was featured on Supergrass's debut album I Should Coco, which reached number one in 1995.

mix.q: In the BBC sitcom The Royle Family, what is the name of Jim and Barbara's daughter played by Caroline Aherne?
mix.why: Caroline Aherne played Denise Royle alongside Ricky Tomlinson as her television father Jim.

mix.q: Which English sea inlet separates the Isle of Wight from the mainland of Great Britain?
mix.why: The Solent is a major shipping lane and host to the annual Cowes Week sailing regatta.

mix.q: Which English pop rock band released the hit album 'Songs from the Big Chair' in 1985?
mix.why: The album spawned huge global hits including 'Everybody Wants to Rule the World' and 'Shout'.

mix.q: In the 1994 action thriller Speed, what speed must the bus stay above to prevent the bomb from detonating?
mix.why: Keanu Reeves and Sandra Bullock had to keep the bus travelling above 50 mph through Los Angeles.

mix.q: Which chemical element has the symbol 'K' on the periodic table?
mix.why: The symbol K comes from Kalium, the Neo-Latin word for potassium derived from Arabic.

mix.q: Which English city was home to Core Design, the video game studio that created Lara Croft?
mix.why: Core Design developed the original Tomb Raider games from their headquarters in Derby.

mix.q: Which Scottish rock band won the 2004 Mercury Prize for their self-titled debut album?
mix.why: Franz Ferdinand took home the Mercury Prize in 2004 following the massive success of 'Take Me Out'.

mix.q: Which fermented condiment was famously created by chemists John Wheeley Lea and William Henry Perrins?
mix.why: Lea & Perrins originally created their signature Worcestershire sauce in Worcester in the 1830s.

mix.q: In the comedy series The Vicar of Dibley, what is the name of the church verger played by Emma Chambers?
mix.why: Emma Chambers won a British Comedy Award in 1998 for her beloved role as Alice Tinker.
